summary: Investigation completed. The latest output at examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation no longer has the prior first-frame dark warm-up flash, but scene_off_flashlight_on remains visually wrong because the scene-off group is already broadly illuminated before/without the requested flashlight contribution. The strongest evidence points to render/light-state leakage from the baseline flashlight and/or persistent render history, with possible residual environment/material lighting; it is not a depth, MP4 encoding, stale-output, or camera-pose issue.
work_completed: Inspected the fresh output directory directly: all four settings contain 240 RGB PNGs, 240 depth NPY frames, 240 viridis depth PNGs, metadata.json, rgb.mp4, and depth_meters_viridis.mp4.

Computed per-frame RGB luma statistics, p99 luma, bright-pixel percentages, adjacent-frame deltas, same-pose loop closure deltas, same-frame cross-condition differences, and depth equality across all settings.
Inspected metadata.json for scene_light_state, scene_lights_enabled, setting state, auto-exposure/render-history flags, and deterministic capture readback state.
Verified MP4 containers with the spear-env OpenCV install: all eight MP4s open as 240 frames at 24 FPS and 1280x720.
Reviewed run_orbit_collection.py render ordering around baseline flashlight spawn, warm-up captures, per-setting command application, and deterministic capture metadata.

findings.message: scene_off_flashlight_off proves the scene-off pass is not dark before the requested flashlight is considered. Its RGB frames are fully visible: median mean luma is 136.29, frame_0000 is 136.30, frame_0239 is 138.82, and representative frame examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation/scene_off_flashlight_off/frames/rgb/frame_0000.png shows the cafeteria lit with no flashlight enabled in metadata. Therefore scene_off_flashlight_on cannot be interpreted as flashlight-only.

scene_off_flashlight_on is bright for the whole sequence, not just frame_0000. Its mean luma min/median/max is 124.51/140.45/152.65, frame_0000 is 141.62, frame_0001 is 140.91, frame_0002 is 140.42, and frame_0239 is 142.13. This rules out the previous first-frame warm-up flash as the current primary failure.

The flashlight setting itself is being applied, but on top of an already-lit scene-off baseline. scene_off_flashlight_on has median p99 luma 246.88 and median pixels >=230 luma of 5.866%, versus scene_off_flashlight_off p99 224.59 and >=230 luma of 0.078%. Same-frame scene_off off->on mean RGB absolute difference is median 12.66 and luma delta median 3.34. Representative path: examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation/scene_off_flashlight_on/frames/rgb/frame_0000.png.

The most suspicious code-level leakage is that run_render_group() spawns and warms the render flashlight with orbit_spec light_baseline_settings before any per-setting command is applied. In the current orbit_spec, baseline is enabled at intensity 1500. Code evidence: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1842 creates baseline_command, :1869-1875 spawns the flashlight with that enabled command, and :1881-1894 discards camera-setup warm-up captures with the baseline command before scene_off_flashlight_off is set at :1920-1922. Because the metadata says render-state persistence was not actually disabled, those baseline-on warm-ups can contaminate the later scene_off_flashlight_off/on captures.

Deterministic capture metadata does not confirm the intended render-history disable. In all four metadata.json files, both rgb and depth_meters report always_persist_rendering_state_disabled=false, dynamic_global_illumination_override_disabled=false, and reflection_override_disabled=false; all persist-property readback attempts have readback=null and verified=false. The command-level disable_render_history=true flag is present, but the component readback says the important state was not verified.

There is residual temporal/noise instability at loop closure even though depth is identical. Frame_0000 and frame_0239 are the same orbit pose; scene_off_flashlight_on has mean absolute luma difference 4.87 with 32.92% of pixels changing by >5 luma, and scene_off_flashlight_off is worse at 8.13 with 53.87% >5. scene_on_flashlight_on is much cleaner at 1.21 and 3.84% >5. This supports persistent render history/noisy lighting state in scene-off outputs, not just normal orbit motion.

Metadata says scene-off disabled 8 light components: visibility_disabled=8, direct_intensity_zeroed=8, indirect_lighting_intensity_zeroed=8, plus one USkyLightComponent with visibility_disabled=1. However environment_contributors.properties_zeroed=0, so the new environment pass did not successfully zero any environment properties. Residual environment/static/material illumination remains a plausible secondary contributor and needs a no-flashlight-ever control to separate it from baseline flashlight history.

Depth and pose are not the cause. All 240 raw depth_meters_npy frames are byte-identical across scene_on_flashlight_off, scene_on_flashlight_on, scene_off_flashlight_off, and scene_off_flashlight_on; all 240 viridis PNGs are also byte-identical across settings. Example depth frame_0000 stats are min 1.0557 m, median 3.2559 m, max 7.0664 m in every setting.

MP4 encoding is not the source. The RGB PNG frames already contain the brightness/noise behavior, and all MP4s open correctly as 240 frames at 24 FPS and 1280x720. The issue is upstream of video writing.

The output does not appear stale. File mtimes show a fresh sequential render on 2026-07-01 local time: scene_on outputs from 15:48:22 through 15:49:10, then scene_off outputs from 15:49:20 through 15:50:07, after the 15:40 Builder result. metadata.json has no per-frame timestamps, so filesystem mtimes are the available frame timing evidence.

scene_on_flashlight_off and scene_on_flashlight_on are nearly identical, indicating the 1500-intensity flashlight is weak relative to scene lights in scene-on mode: same-frame mean RGB absolute difference median 1.90, luma delta median 0.017, and median mean luma is about 151.0 in both.

follow_up_recommendations: Builder should stop using orbit_spec light_baseline_settings for render-mode setup warm-up. In run_render_group(), choose an initial render command from the first setting in that scene-light group, or spawn the flashlight disabled until the first setting is applied. For scene-off groups, scene_off_flashlight_off must have a mode where the flashlight has never been enabled before its captures or warm-ups.

Builder should make render-history disabling verifiable or fail fast. If --disable-render-history is active, metadata should show bAlwaysPersistRenderingState disabled for each capture component or the script should report that deterministic capture is unsupported. Inspect the USpSceneCaptureComponent2D Python/C++ property name or add an explicit setter/readback API.

Builder should add a hard diagnostic setting or separate render group named no_flashlight_ever/scene_off_no_flashlight_ever that disables scene lights and never spawns/enables the spotlight. If that render is still bright, the root cause is environment/static/material lighting; if it is dark, the current failure is baseline flashlight/render-history leakage.

Builder should add automated PNG-output validation after render: scene_off_flashlight_off median mean luma should be near black for flashlight-only validation; frame_0000->frame_0001 and frame_0239->frame_0000 same-pose luma deltas should be bounded; depth must remain identical across settings; scene_off_flashlight_on should differ from scene_off_flashlight_off mainly in a localized beam mask.

If no_flashlight_ever remains bright, repair the map/render environment rather than the per-setting flashlight logic: remove or black out emissive materials and sky/backdrop materials for flashlight-only validation, disable/zero skylight and post-process ambient properties with verified readback, use a map variant with no baked/precomputed lighting, and keep scene lights movable/dynamic only.

Record renderer CVar/readback metadata for the deterministic INI assumptions, especially Lumen GI/reflections, SSR, TAA, motion blur, eye adaptation, and capture persistent render state, so future investigations do not have to infer whether those settings actually took effect.
memory_worthy: Latest orbit_collection_output_validation on 2026-07-01 shows first-frame warm-up flash is fixed, but scene_off_flashlight_off is still bright, scene_off_flashlight_on is bright throughout, deterministic capture readback is false, and run_render_group warms with the baseline flashlight enabled before per-setting scene-off captures.
